observation_summary: The SummaryStatistics class fails to correctly update overridden mean, variance, or geometric mean implementations when values are added, resulting in NaN values for these statistics.
hypothesis: The conditional checks in the addValue method incorrectly use 'instanceof' to determine if the implementation has been overridden. If a user provides an instance of the default class (e.g., 'new Variance(false)'), the 'instanceof' check returns true, causing the code to skip the necessary 'increment' call on the overridden implementation.
prediction: Changing the conditional checks from '!(impl instanceof DefaultClass)' to 'impl != defaultInstance' will ensure that the custom implementation is correctly updated even if it is an instance of the default class.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the logic was changed from checking the type (instanceof) to checking object identity (reference equality). This confirms that the original logic was failing to identify when an implementation was overridden by an instance of the same class.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect conditional check (predicate logic) in the addValue method. The code was using 'instanceof' to decide whether to update the statistics implementation, which failed when the user provided an instance of the same class as the default. Changing this to a reference equality check correctly validates whether the implementation is the default one or a custom override, which is a classic 'Checking' defect.
evidence_used: The bug report description explicitly states: 'The problem in the SummaryStatistics code is in addValue: if (!(meanImpl instanceof Mean)) { ... }'
The fix_diff_oracle shows the change from 'if (!(meanImpl instanceof Mean))' to 'if (meanImpl != mean)'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is procedural, the root cause is specifically the incorrect predicate used to guard the update operation, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
